REQUIREMENT SLUG: ipc-multi-connection-throughput
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/ipc-multi-connection-throughput.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/ipc-multi-connection-throughput.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: ipc-multi-connection-throughput" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/ipc-multi-connection-throughput.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/ipc-multi-connection-throughput.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.
  * IMPORTANT - a previous interrupted run left some UNCOMMITTED work in this tree. Before you start, run `cd /workspace && git status --short` and inspect `git diff` for the files you expect to touch. If part or all of this requirement is already implemented in the working tree but not yet committed, do NOT redo it from scratch: review it critically, finish/correct anything missing or wrong, then stage exactly those paths and commit as above. That uncommitted work is yours to claim when it belongs to this slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):

title: HADOOP-13144. Enhancing IPC client throughput via multiple connections per user
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Hadoop service running very high IPC call volumes to the same endpoint can bottleneck on a single client-side connection per user, even when the workload itself is highly parallel.


  ## Desired outcome

  Operators and framework code should be able to open more than one logical client connection for the same address, protocol, and user when they deliberately vary the connection identity, instead of being forced through one shared channel. The public RPC surface needs to make that possible by accepting a caller-supplied `Client.ConnectionId` in `RPC.getProtocolProxy(...)`, so advanced clients can spread traffic without forking the whole RPC stack.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using `RPC.getProtocolProxy` with distinct `Client.ConnectionId` instances should yield independent client proxies and allow the same principal to drive parallel request streams to one server. Existing call semantics, security initialization, and retry behavior from the `ConnectionId` must remain intact.

  '

package org.apache.hadoop.ipc;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.net.InetSocketAddress;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;

import javax.net.SocketFactory;

import org.apache.hadoop.classification.InterfaceStability;
import org.apache.hadoop.conf.Configuration;
import org.apache.hadoop.io.retry.RetryPolicy;
import org.apache.hadoop.ipc.Client.ConnectionId;
import org.apache.hadoop.security.UserGroupInformation;
import org.apache.hadoop.security.token.SecretManager;
import org.apache.hadoop.security.token.TokenIdentifier;

/** An RPC implementation. */
@InterfaceStability.Evolving
public interface RpcEngine {

  /** Construct a client-side proxy object. 
   * @param <T>*/
  <T> ProtocolProxy<T> getProxy(Class<T> protocol,
                  long clientVersion, InetSocketAddress addr,
                  UserGroupInformation ticket, Configuration conf,
                  SocketFactory factory, int rpcTimeout,
                  RetryPolicy connectionRetryPolicy) throws IOException;

  /** Construct a client-side proxy object. */
  <T> ProtocolProxy<T> getProxy(Class<T> protocol,
                  long clientVersion, InetSocketAddress addr,
                  UserGroupInformation ticket, Configuration conf,
                  SocketFactory factory, int rpcTimeout,
                  RetryPolicy connectionRetryPolicy,
                  AtomicBoolean fallbackToSimpleAuth,
                  AlignmentContext alignmentContext) throws IOException;

  /** 
   * Construct a server for a protocol implementation instance.
   * 
   * @param protocol the class of protocol to use
   * @param instance the instance of protocol whose methods will be called
   * @param conf the configuration to use
   * @param bindAddress the address to bind on to listen for connection
   * @param port the port to listen for connections on
   * @param numHandlers the number of method handler threads to run
   * @param numReaders the number of reader threads to run
   * @param queueSizePerHandler the size of the queue per hander thread
   * @param verbose whether each call should be logged
   * @param secretManager The secret manager to use to validate incoming requests.
   * @param portRangeConfig A config parameter that can be used to restrict
   *        the range of ports used when port is 0 (an ephemeral port)
   * @param alignmentContext provides server state info on client responses
   * @return The Server instance
   * @throws IOException on any error
   */
  RPC.Server getServer(Class<?> protocol, Object instance, String bindAddress,
                       int port, int numHandlers, int numReaders,
                       int queueSizePerHandler, boolean verbose,
                       Configuration conf, 
                       SecretManager<? extends TokenIdentifier> secretManager,
                       String portRangeConfig,
                       AlignmentContext alignmentContext) throws IOException;

  /**
   * Returns a proxy for ProtocolMetaInfoPB, which uses the given connection
   * id.
   * @param connId, ConnectionId to be used for the proxy.
   * @param conf, Configuration.
   * @param factory, Socket factory.
   * @return Proxy object.
   * @throws IOException
   */
  ProtocolProxy<ProtocolMetaInfoPB> getProtocolMetaInfoProxy(
      ConnectionId connId, Configuration conf, SocketFactory factory)
      throws IOException;
}
